title: Labels or Input? Rethinking Augmentation in Multimodal Hate Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model robustness against spurious correlations by testing on an extended dataset of counterfactually neutral memes that retain racial terms (e.g., 'Black') in benign contexts, and using category-specific prompts defining racism and white supremacy.

Measuring classification performance on augmented, non-hateful memes that explicitly contain religious identity terms (e.g., 'Muslims') to ensure the model does not automatically associate these terms with hate speech, supplemented by categorical prompts defining anti-Muslim and anti-Semitic hate.

Evaluating debiasing strategies by generating counterfactually neutral memes that mention gender-related terms (e.g., 'Women') to test if models over-predict toxicity, alongside prompting frameworks that explicitly define misogyny and sexism.

Using counterfactual multimodal augmentation to neutralize meme captions targeting immigrants and specific nationalities, assessing whether models can distinguish between benign mentions of immigrants and actual xenophobia.

Applying category-based structured prompts that define homophobia and transphobia to evaluate and improve the vision-language model's ability to detect targeted anti-LGBTQ+ hate speech without relying on spurious cues.

Utilizing granular prompt definitions to guide models in identifying derogatory language and mockery directed at people with physical or mental disabilities, differentiating it from non-hateful content.
Testing the model's classification of political hate speech using structured prompts that outline inflammatory language or rhetoric designed to polarize based on political beliefs.
